rules.source_statement: Chapter XLVIII asks whether a servant shall gain freedom from his master; it begins only after the divider separating Chapter XLVII.
preconditions: Historical horary question regarding service or slavery.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source social relation is from the 1647 text, not an endorsement or contemporary legal model.

rules.source_statement: The first house, its lord and the Moon are assigned to signify the servant in this question.
preconditions: Use a chart erected for the question.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: These represent the servant; do not substitute the master's tenth-house lord.

rules.source_statement: The tenth house and lord of its sign denote the master, whatever his social condition.
preconditions: Same service question and its tenth house.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The author's 'let his condition be what it will' must not be collapsed into a class restriction.

rules.source_statement: Examine joining of the ascendant's lord to the tenth lord and whether the author calls it a perfect conjunction, whether by body or aspect, with or without reception.
preconditions: Compare these two specific significators; evaluate body/aspect and reception independently.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The text's broad use of 'conjunction ... by body or aspect' is retained without imposing a narrower modern technical definition.

rules.source_statement: If the joining is exact by degree and minute, the servant is said to gain freedom easily and in a short time.
preconditions: The conjunction between first-house lord and tenth-house lord is perfect to degree and minute.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Both exactness and the two designated lords matter; not every contact means immediate release.

rules.source_statement: If the ascendant lord has separated from the tenth lord by only a few minutes, Lilly treats the servant as effectively freed already.
preconditions: A recent separation of a few minutes, not an applying conjunction.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source describes an inference from already separating geometry; does not document an actual release.

rules.source_statement: If no such joining or aspect occurs between the two lords, apply the same method to the Moon as substitute servant significator.
preconditions: First lord–tenth lord contact is absent.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The Moon must make the same relevant aspect; no automatic positive result from mere presence.

rules.source_statement: If neither the Moon nor first-house lord separates from the tenth lord, Lilly next examines whether either separates from or joins the Sun, judging by similar aspect conditions.
preconditions: Both prior comparisons fail; distinguish separation from joining with the Sun.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source introduces a second fallback to Sun; not an unconditional 'Sun means freedom' rule.

rules.source_statement: The text distinguishes a determinate from an absolute question and contrasts release from this particular master now with ever gaining freedom from his power.
preconditions: Identify whether the query concerns a specific current master or freedom more generally.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The author's 'determinate and not absolute' phrasing is ambiguous with the paired examples and should be preserved, not silently repaired.

rules.source_statement: For the specified question, a first-house lord cadent from an angle and lacking an aspect to the ascendant is given as a condition predicting departure from service.
preconditions: Source combines cadency from an angle with no ascendant aspect.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Alternative source configurations follow; do not reclassify the whole preceding contact logic.

rules.source_statement: A first-house lord in aspect to a planet occupying an angle, or with a planet that beholds the ascendant, is another configuration offered for gaining freedom.
preconditions: Planet in angle OR one that beholds ascendant; first lord aspect must exist.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The phrase allows alternatives; no claim that a particular angular position alone proves the outcome.

rules.source_statement: The first-house lord located in the third or ninth house, or joined to a planet in either, is offered as a sign the servant will depart.
preconditions: Third/ninth placement OR conjunction with a planet located there.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: These are alternative placements, not one obligatory composite aspect.

rules.source_statement: The same departure reasoning is allowed from the Moon if its aspects supply the corresponding conditions.
preconditions: Moon must exhibit analogous aspects or configurations to those just listed.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not count Moon and ascendant-lord as independent observed servant outcomes.

rules.source_statement: If Moon or ascendant lord is in the ascendant, tenth, seventh or fourth, or joined to a planet in one of those angles, and that planet is direct, the servant is said not to be delivered.
preconditions: Specify Moon/ascendant lord or joined angular planet; the stated planetary directness is essential.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The conditional starts at printed296 bottom and continues printed297; preserve all four angular houses.

rules.source_statement: If that aforesaid angular planet is retrograde instead of direct, the text allows freedom but with slowness and difficulty.
preconditions: The same angular-planet scenario, with retrograde motion substituting for direct motion.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This qualifies the previous negative; retrogradation changes direction and tempo, not proof of actual freedom.

rules.source_statement: When the ascendant lord in the angles is impeded by corporeal conjunction with an ill planet, freedom from service is denied.
preconditions: Ascendant lord afflicted in 1st/10th/7th/4th by conjunction to malefic.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The house and affliction conditions belong together; separate from the generic principle of angular proximity.

rules.source_statement: In the same angular impediment clause, a square or opposition from an ill planet to the ascendant lord also denies release.
preconditions: Angular first-house lord; malefic square or opposition.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Both adverse aspect kinds are alternatives within one historical prohibition.

rules.source_statement: If the first-house lord in the stated angular context is entering combustion, Lilly also denies freedom from that service.
preconditions: Entering (applying to) combustion, not simply any Sun placement.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source says 'entring combustion'; current combust and entering combustion are not interchangeable.

rules.source_statement: The phrase Finis Sexæ Domus marks the end of the sixth-house treatment immediately after XLVIII and before the seventh-house introduction.
preconditions: Structural source boundary on printed297.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not a new numbered house theory or separate servant success event.

rules.source_statement: The unnumbered heading The Significations of the seventh House begins the next house-topic introduction.
preconditions: Starts below the end-of-sixth-house line and ornamental rule.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The heading is NOT Chapter XLIX and is not one of the forty-three aphorisms.

rules.source_statement: The seventh-house heading lists marriage, open enemies, lawsuits, controversies, contracts, wars, bargains, fugitives and thefts.
preconditions: Original seventh-house topic list is on printed297.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This enumerates 1647 topics, not validated associations or distinct observations.

rules.source_statement: Lilly says questions naturally belonging to the seventh house demand more consideration and are more difficult to judge than those of any other house.
preconditions: Applies to the seventh-house class of questions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is an authorial methodological claim, not measured predictive difficulty.

rules.source_statement: The author says this difficulty required a larger exposition of opinions from both ancient authorities and some modern practitioners.
preconditions: Rationale for the following enlarged material.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No independently enumerated source citations supplied here; not a primary-source collation of the named people.

rules.source_statement: The introduction announces forty-three significant aphorisms, said to illuminate seventh-house matters and the broader body of astrology.
preconditions: Announcement explicitly says forty-three and broad application.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not conflate these forty-three general horary aphorisms with the earlier forty-three physician aphorisms in chapter XLIV.

rules.source_statement: The separate unnumbered heading Aphorismes and Considerations for better judging any Horary Question introduces the 43 numbered rules.
preconditions: This heading occurs on PDF332/printed298 before aphorism 1.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Treat as general horary advice and seventh-house prefatory material, not a new numbered Chapter.

rules.source_statement: Before judging, test whether the question is radical or fit to be judged by agreement in nature or triplicity between the ascendant lord and the planetary hour lord.
preconditions: Lord of ascendant and lord of hour must be of one nature OR same triplicity.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source gives a radicality check, not proof the question is objectively answerable.

rules.source_statement: Warn against confident judgment when the earliest or latest degrees of any sign are ascending; early may mean premature, late may mean matter passed, prior tampering or despair.
preconditions: Both early and late rising degrees are cautions, with DIFFERENT reasons.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The late-degree account is probable/possible rather than confirmed misconduct; advise not to meddle at that time.

rules.source_statement: Saturn or Mars in tenth and peregrine/unfortunate, or the dragon-tail-like node in tenth, threatens the astrologer's credit from the question.
preconditions: Planet must occupy the tenth with the stated bad condition, OR node in tenth.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The node glyph is copy-specific; do not silently replace with a different node or apply to all houses.

rules.source_statement: Avoid judgment on trivial, lightly motivated or unpremeditated questions, or when the querent does not understand what is being asked.
preconditions: Applies to insufficient reflection, trivial demand, or inability to formulate question.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: An admonition concerning method; not a diagnostic judgment about a person.

rules.source_statement: Give particular weight to the Moon's strength or debility; Lilly prefers misfortune of ascendant lord to misfortune of Moon because she conveys the other planets' strength and virtue.
preconditions: Assessment of Moon is central in every horary question.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Moon as transmitter of virtue is a source assumption, not observational causal evidence.

rules.source_statement: Saturn is described as naturally adverse through excessive cold and Mars through excessive heat, signifying delay/detriment unless significators mutually receive one another.
preconditions: Conditional Saturn/Mars significators; mitigation requires reciprocal reception.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Lilly explicitly says their physical nature is not literally cold/dry; treat as virtue/operation, not measured physical temperature.

rules.source_statement: Jupiter and Venus are natural fortunes, with malice only by accident; where they are significators, strongest performance is through applying sextile or trine and essential dignity.
preconditions: Benefic significators, applications by sextile/trine and essential dignity; absence of reception matters.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Without reception benefics may advance but not perform as fully; do not equate inherently benefic with unconditional success.

rules.source_statement: Where fortunes are significators, expect favourable result; where infortunes, fear unfavourable, and order conduct accordingly.
preconditions: Class of main significator is favourable/unfavourable in this historic scheme.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is a general heuristic with later conditions limiting it, not a calibrated chance.

rules.source_statement: A void-of-course Moon suggests little hope, but in Cancer, Taurus, Sagittarius or Pisces this impediment is lessened.
preconditions: Moon void of course; stated FOUR signs qualify the negative.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Preserve all four exceptions; do not call void course necessarily fatal to the question.

rules.source_statement: The planet from which Moon separates is taken to describe what has already occurred; a benefic separation suggests good, a malefic bad, qualified by the relevant house.
preconditions: Moon separating from an identified planet; inspect nature and house.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is a past-event signification, not the present application or future prediction.

rules.source_statement: The Moon's application signifies present condition; good application/aspect, good house and good planet collectively signify strong hope for the intended matter.
preconditions: Moon applying by good aspect AND to good planet in good house.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not collapse a composite favourable condition into any application.

rules.source_statement: Application of Moon to a planet in that planet's fall signifies anguish, trouble and delay.
preconditions: Moon APPLYING to a planet located in its FALL.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: A planet's fall and Moon application are prerequisites; not any fallen planet anywhere.

rules.source_statement: A retrograde significator or a significator in its first station denotes discord and much contradiction.
preconditions: Planet is significator and is retrograde OR in first station.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not conflate first station with second station or any slow motion.

rules.source_statement: When an evil planet is significator, forecast evil may be more severe; forecast good may be less than expected, imperfect and achieved only with heavy solicitation and affliction.
preconditions: Adverse planet must be significator; negative versus positive predictions have different branches.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The author permits difficult partial good rather than categorical no result.

rules.source_statement: A planet slow in motion is said to prolong the matter; the sign in which it sits helps qualify the delay.
preconditions: Relevant planet is slow in motion; interpret sign nature.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: A delay claim, not automatic failure; source says matter is hardly performed.

rules.source_statement: If infortunes signify an evil, favourable Jupiter or Venus aspects may lessen that evil; the final phrase 'do so when the Fortunes are Significators' is a separate underexplained extension.
preconditions: Evil indicated by infortune significator AND a Fortune casting aspect; consider signification reversals separately.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No unambiguous rule for the final do-so clause is supplied; preserve instead of inventing a fully symmetrical algorithm.

rules.source_statement: Benefic significators in cadent houses, poor essential dignity, without aspect to ascendant or retrograde are impeded and accomplish little unless received.
preconditions: One or more bad placements of fortunes; reception is explicit exception.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not a global rule that Jupiter/Venus always fail, and reception qualifies it.

rules.source_statement: Even with reception an infortune is said to perform little, while in the same circumstances a fortune as significator can perfect the matter.
preconditions: Reception present; compare infortune to benefic SIGNIFICATOR.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source's contrast is between malefic/benefic under reception, not simply presence.

rules.source_statement: A peregrine planet with no essential dignities is said to behave maliciously; essential dignity makes it less so; Lilly uses an analogy of an enemy controlled by a noble person.
preconditions: No essential dignity versus dignity present.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not convert peregrine condition into a diagnosis of malice in real humans.

rules.source_statement: Generally Saturn or Mars in house, exaltation or triplicity AND angles are said to perform a desired matter, notwithstanding their usual negative reputations.
preconditions: Malefic is in an essential dignity category AND an angle, and has significator role.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The phrase spans printed299–300; separate essential status from angular placement.

rules.source_statement: Do not rely heavily on a fortune's assistance without its essential dignity; full performance when dignified, only half otherwise.
preconditions: A beneficial planet assisting a question; compare essential dignity.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Half is source figurative completion language, not a precise 50% probability.

rules.source_statement: If fortunes and infortunes are both weak or comparably ill-placed, promise no success and postpone judgment until a better celestial configuration.
preconditions: Both classes weak OR equally badly situated.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The instruction is to defer judgment in this historical method; not forecast unavoidable failure.

rules.source_statement: A combust significator or a significator opposing the Sun is treated as unable to bring the matter to perfection.
preconditions: The planet must signify the QUESTION and be combust OR in solar opposition.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No unqualified claim that all planets in opposition imply absolute failure.

rules.source_statement: Two infortunes joined: even a favourable indication from their aspect is said to come to nothing; adverse indication may be worse than expected.
preconditions: Conjunction of two malefics, then distinguish good- and bad-signified cases.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The evil outcome is described as probable, not certain.

rules.source_statement: Ascendant lord out of essential dignities AND cadent signals loss of querent's hope in the matter.
preconditions: Lord of ascendant, lacking essential dignity and cadent house, with 'etc.' nonexhaustive.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Separate this source's pessimism from objectively observed mental states.

rules.source_statement: Within twelve degrees of Sun the planet is described as under Sun's beams and lacking strength; within sixteen arcminutes of Sun is cazimi, exceptionally strong.
preconditions: Different angular thresholds: 12 degrees for under beams; 16 MINUTES for cazimi.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Treat source-specific threshold literally; do not substitute a later 17-minute definition.

rules.source_statement: Dispositor's oriental/occidental status affects timing: Saturn/Jupiter/Mars oriental suggests earlier performance and occidental later; reverse the timing for Venus/Mercury.
preconditions: First identify the planet receiving significator's disposition, then planetary group and oriental/occidental status.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The opposite timing rule for the second group is essential, not a universal east=sooner formula.

rules.source_statement: Fixed signs signify stability/continuance; common signs likelihood of perfection without conclusion; movable signs swift resolution either way; Lilly associates fixed with building, movable with journeys and common with desired moderation.
preconditions: Relevant matter's significator in FIXED, COMMON or MOVABLE sign, with differing contexts.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not transform all three categories into an ordinal probability or guaranteed outcome.

rules.source_statement: Ascendant lord or Moon with Head or Tail of Dragon is said to damage the question; inspect house in which the node is situated.
preconditions: Either designated significator contacts EITHER named node; identify the house.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source does not automatically make north node beneficial here; the rule crosses page334–335.

rules.source_statement: A pending eclipse at the ascendant's degree or at the sign-degree occupied by significator is said to harm a seemingly promising matter unexpectedly.
preconditions: Degree alignment with an eclipse at hand; either ascendant degree or significator location.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is explicitly future eclipse contingency, not any eclipse anywhere.

rules.source_statement: An impeded Moon brings obstruction; if waning, source warns for querent's life, with separate ill journey and ill wooing/marriage examples.
preconditions: Moon impeded, with added waning condition for life concern and topic-specific interpretations.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical warning is not medical, travel safety or relationship advice.

rules.source_statement: The lord of the question or Moon in a sign opposite to own house means low hopes, despair or indifference toward completion; Mercury in Sagittarius or Pisces is the source example.
preconditions: Relevant significator in sign opposite own domicile; the text supplies Mercury in Sagittarius/Pisces as an example.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not mistake a sign *opposite the seventh house* for the sign opposite planet's own house.

rules.source_statement: Identify a planet obstructing the desired significator and read both its ruled house and occupied house to investigate who or what obstructs.
preconditions: A particular planet actually impedes the thing's significator; inspect house rulership or location.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The two house associations are alternative evidence channels, not certain identification of a human offender.

rules.source_statement: Closer placement of significator to an angle is described as better; succedent less and cadent little.
preconditions: Relative house angularity of the actual significator.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not a numeric linear scale or universal rule irrespective of planetary condition.

rules.source_statement: Moon's conjunction to Sun/combustion is described as its worst affliction, stronger than other negative aspects from infortunes.
preconditions: The Moon conjunct the Sun; compare adverse significations.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not call all solar aspects combustion or infer a safe medical conclusion.

rules.source_statement: An infortune aspects the significator and both planets may be peregrine, retrograde, cadent or in contrary-nature signs, suggesting potentially unavoidable mischief under natural causes.
preconditions: Both aspect between infortune and significator AND one of the stated bad-status conditions (the source's grouping is uncertain).
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Phrases 'may then be doubted' and 'according to natural causes' qualify inevitability.

rules.source_statement: Two significators conjunct AND in a sign agreeing with their own nature bring easy perfection; otherwise not.
preconditions: Two relevant significators joined by conjunction and sign suits their nature.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: An unqualified conjunction alone is not sufficient.

rules.source_statement: Before the perfecting aspect, investigate frustration or prohibition; the frustrating planet signifies a party or cause hindering the matter.
preconditions: Potential frustration/prohibition occurs BEFORE perfection of relevant aspect.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep temporal order and identify the specific intervening planet.

rules.source_statement: A well-dignified Part-of-Fortune-like glyph in a house is associated with benefit from that house's persons or things, ill-dignified with damage.
preconditions: Part-of-Fortune-like glyph identity and dignity and placement in a particular house.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Copy glyph identity requires source-image qualification; no benefit amount or certainty given.

rules.source_statement: In marriage questions a malefic in seventh is said to threaten disagreement UNLESS that same planet is a significator at birth.
preconditions: Marriage question; an infortune occupies seventh; check natal-significator exception.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The birth-chart exception is source-explicit and independent from the question's seventh-house designation.

rules.source_statement: Eighth-house lord impeded/unfortunate IN the eighth predicts loss through death of some woman OR debt owed by deceased men.
preconditions: Lord of the eighth located within eighth AND afflicted; distinguish woman-death and debt branches.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No empirical validation of death, gender association or estate debt.

rules.source_statement: Well-dignified Jupiter and Venus in any house suggest gain from its people/things; examples third from kin, fourth from father/lands, fifth from play, others by house.
preconditions: Jupiter AND Venus are well-dignified in specified house; source's 'and' may be a generic conjunction listing benefics rather than requiring co-location.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep exact house-derived benefit conditions and avoid overrestricting both planets to one house if not warranted.

rules.source_statement: Beware people and affairs of the house containing the printed Dragon Tail (south-node-like) glyph; author predicts damage, scandal or slander.
preconditions: The named glyph is in a specific house; interpret by that house's topics.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original glyph and risk terms are source-specific; not verified misconduct or harm.

rules.source_statement: Chapter XLIX, Of Marriage, begins BELOW the divider on original PDF336/printed302, immediately after aphorism 43; it is not extracted in this batch.
preconditions: Boundary follows the forty-third horary aphorism.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Marriage chapter arguments on PDF336 lower and PDF337 onward are not part of B02r.
